cache_implementation_discovered.summary: Re-verified from source (not from the B1 summary alone). The cache-hit substitution, revalidation, and provider-call-avoidance logic already exists in full, correct, tested form in comqutor_alpha/llm_runtime/session.py (SemanticRuntimeSession.start_call/finalize_call) and comqutor_alpha/structure_engine/week2_llm.py (Week2LLMGateway._start_semantic_call/invoke_json_with_trace). The ONLY missing piece was a real cache backend ever being constructed and passed in -- every production call site left this at the default None, which resolves to NullLLMResponseCache (always-miss).
cache_implementation_discovered.session_read_path: SemanticRuntimeSession.start_call calls self.cache.get(cache_key), validates the entry via validate_cache_entry, checks identity fields (task/prompt_sha256/input_sha256/provider/model/output_schema_version) match exactly, and only then sets trace.cache_hit=True and returns the cached validated_output.
cache_implementation_discovered.session_write_path: SemanticRuntimeSession.finalize_call computes cache_eligible = (validation_status=='accepted' and provider_status=='success' and accepted_candidate is not None and not fallback_used and not trace.cache_hit and not self.incomplete) and only calls self.cache.put(...) when eligible -- a fallback, rejected, or already-cache-hit record is never written back.
cache_implementation_discovered.gateway_substitution_path: Week2LLMGateway.invoke_json_with_trace: on a cache hit, the cached candidate is re-run through the SAME validator callable used for a live response; on success it returns Week2LLMInvocation(cache_hit=True, provider_called=False, provider_status='not_called', retry_count=0, provider_attempt_count=0) WITHOUT calling the Provider. On cache-candidate revalidation failure, it fails OPEN to a live Provider call (never fails the run, never returns corrupted data).
cache_implementation_discovered.manifest_accounting_path: comqutor_alpha/llm_runtime/manifest.py: build_semantic_manifest computes cache_hit_count = sum(record.cache.hit) and provider_call_count = sum(1+retry_count for records where provider_status in PROVIDER_CALLED_STATUSES) -- a cache-hit record's provider_status='not_called' already correctly excludes it from provider_call_count. This existed before this task and required zero changes.

scope_selected.cache_scope: RUN_LOCAL (in-process, in-memory, one fresh instance per run_research_request call)
scope_selected.reasoning: B1 measured a negligible cross-run exact-duplicate opportunity (2 of 3684 alpha_classifier calls, ~0.05%) versus a real, measurable within-run opportunity (0-6.36% of alpha_classifier calls per run). A persistent cross-run cache would add staleness/invalidation/deployment/storage/version-lifecycle complexity for almost no measured benefit -- explicitly avoided per instruction. run_research_request is called exactly once per research run (verified via its sole caller, research_lifecycle.execute_claimed_research_run) -- a cache instance constructed inside that call is therefore correctly and simply run-local by construction, with no extra scoping logic needed.
scope_selected.existing_production_ready_backend_consid: RedisLLMResponseCache exists and is production-ready, but requires an injected Redis-like client -- introducing an external service dependency for a measured ~1.1% aggregate call-reduction opportunity is explicitly the persistent-cache complexity this slice avoids. A new InMemoryLLMResponseCache class was added to the SAME file (comqutor_alpha/llm_runtime/cache.py), using the exact same LLMResponseCache protocol, build_llm_cache_key, and validate_cache_entry/LLMCacheEntry contract as RedisLLMResponseCache -- no new cache subsystem, no new external dependency, no new file added to comqutor_alpha/llm_runtime/ (which has its own test asserting an exact file list).

cache_failure_behavior.detail: Verified from existing, unmodified code: SemanticRuntimeSession.start_call catches CacheCorruptionError and any other cache.get() exception, marks the session degraded (not failed), and returns a trace with cached_candidate=None -- indistinguishable from a plain cache miss to the caller, which then proceeds to a live Provider call. Week2LLMGateway.invoke_json_with_trace additionally re-validates a returned cached candidate through the real task validator; if that revalidation itself fails, it also falls through to a live Provider call. A cache.put() failure in finalize_call is caught and marked degraded, without failing the run or returning corrupted data. This slice introduces zero new failure-handling logic -- it inherits the already-correct fail-open behavior by using the same LLMResponseCache Protocol and the same session/gateway call paths.

concurrent_duplicate_investigation.question: Can alpha_classifier's existing concurrency=4 cause two identical-content calls to be genuinely in-flight simultaneously, requiring single-flight coalescing rather than a simple completed-response cache?
concurrent_duplicate_investigation.method: Replayed each persisted run's llm_semantic_calls.jsonl in call_sequence order; for every repeated cache_key, checked whether the later occurrence's started_at was at or after the earlier occurrence's completed_at (simple-cache-eligible) or strictly before it (would require single-flight coalescing to avoid).
concurrent_duplicate_investigation.result: ZERO in-flight-only duplicates found in any of the seven analyzed runs -- every single repeated cache_key's later occurrence started strictly after the earlier occurrence had already completed. A simple completed-response cache captures the ENTIRE measured duplicate-call opportunity; single-flight coalescing is not needed for this measured duplicate set.
concurrent_duplicate_investigation.conclusion: Single-flight coalescing is explicitly NOT implemented in this slice -- documented as a possible Slice 1B/later optimization only if a future run's duplicate pattern actually requires it (none observed to date).

offline_cache_simulation.method: For each persisted run, replayed llm_semantic_calls.jsonl in call_sequence order using the run's own already-recorded cache.cache_key field (not recomputed) and its own already-recorded eligibility fields (validation_status/provider_status/fallback_used/validated_output), simulating exactly the same cache_eligible rule SemanticRuntimeSession.finalize_call already enforces. No Provider call was made; this is a pure offline replay of existing persisted data.
offline_cache_simulation.comparison_against_b1: B1 reported 35/2/1/7/2/0/0 exact within-run alpha_classifier duplicates for QQQ_postfix/QQQ_historical/MSFT/SNDK/TSM/AMD/NVDA respectively. This simulation's simple_hits column reproduces those exact same figures for every run (35/2/1/7/2/0/0) -- CONFIRMED, no unexpected difference. All duplication in every run is concentrated in alpha_classifier; zero duplicates were found in structured_adapter, evidence_stance_classifier, or structure_extractor in any run, in either B1 or this replay.

qqq_offline_cache_simulation_detail.note: All 35 B1-theoretical duplicate calls ARE eliminable by a simple completed-response cache -- confirmed by actual call-ordering replay, not assumed.

output_equivalence.method: For every simulated cache hit, compared the record's own validated_output_sha256 against the sha256 the simulation's cache had stored for that cache_key (from the FIRST occurrence).
output_equivalence.result_summary: 33 of 35 QQQ post-fix cache-eligible duplicates show validated_output_sha256 IDENTICAL between the historical first and later occurrence -- 0 output difference. 2 of 35 show a DIFFERENT validated_output_sha256 between the two historical (uncached) calls.

critical_disclosure_the_two_output_diffe.finding: For 2 of the 550 alpha_classifier calls in the QQQ post-fix run, the historical system independently invoked the LLM TWICE for byte-identical input (same claim, same taxonomy, same everything -- same cache_key) and received GENUINELY DIFFERENT decisions both times. Example 1: call_sequence 684 returned {'decision':'select','selected_alpha_id':'A304'} while call_sequence 728 (identical input) returned {'decision':'none','selected_alpha_id':None}. Example 2: call_sequence 698 returned {'decision':'none','selected_alpha_id':None} while call_sequence 742 (identical input) returned {'decision':'select','selected_alpha_id':'A301'}.
critical_disclosure_the_two_output_diffe.root_cause: Inherent LLM sampling non-determinism -- a pre-existing characteristic of the deepseek-v4-flash provider/model, not a defect introduced by this cache slice, and not something the cache-key design (or any cache design) can or should try to hide.
critical_disclosure_the_two_output_diffe.effect_of_enabling_the_cache: With the cache enabled, the SECOND occurrence of each of these 2 duplicate pairs would be served the FIRST occurrence's answer instead of independently re-querying the model -- i.e. caching necessarily 'locks in' one of the model's two possible answers for a repeat of identical content, trading away this specific (rare) variance for determinism and fewer calls.
critical_disclosure_the_two_output_diffe.scope_of_this_disclosure: 2 of 617 real historical provider calls in QQQ post-fix (0.32% of all calls; 2 of 35 simple-cache-eligible duplicates, 5.7% of the duplicates themselves). Zero such instability was found in the other six runs' (much smaller) duplicate sets.
critical_disclosure_the_two_output_diffe.gold_acceptance_impact_check: Directly verified against QQQ post-fix's own run_audit.json: A304 reached 'active' with 58 raw supporting claims / 38 unique evidence facts, and A301 reached 'active' with 17 raw supporting claims / 9 unique evidence facts -- a single claim's presence or absence in either pool does not change either Alpha's detected level. This disclosure does not change any QQQ post-fix Gold-acceptance-sensitive outcome (A304/A301 detection, dominant status, or main conflict all remain exactly as already adjudicated in v0_2_six_run_gold_conformance_audit.json).
critical_disclosure_the_two_output_diffe.disposition: Disclosed as a transparency item for John's awareness, NOT treated as a defect in this cache implementation (which is behaving exactly as an exact-match cache is designed to: return a previously-valid answer for byte-identical repeat input) and NOT something this slice is authorized or scoped to adjudicate or fix (would require prompt/model/sampling changes, explicitly out of scope). Flagged as a candidate topic for a future, separately-scoped 'LLM output stability' investigation -- not blocking this slice's PASS decision.
